chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Ali ibn Ja'far, who said:
'I heard Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) saying:'
'Not everyone who speaks as being with our Wilayah is a Momin. But, it has been Made to be a comfort for the Momineen.'

key_terms.أُنْساً: comfort, companionship, or familiarity — a source of solace and social ease for the true believers
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the Momineen — the genuine, inwardly confirmed believers as distinct from those who merely profess
key_terms.بِوَلَايَتِنَا: with our Wilayah — the acknowledgment of and allegiance to the divinely appointed authority and guardianship of the Imams (peace be upon them)
key_terms.جُعِلُوا: they have been Made (passive) — divinely designated or ordained, indicating a decree from Allah
key_terms.مُؤْمِناً: a Momin — a true believer whose faith has penetrated the heart, surpassing outward profession

ai.seo_question: Does verbally professing wilayah to the Imams (peace be upon them) make one a true Momin according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) draws a critical distinction between outward verbal profession of wilayah (allegiance and guardianship of the Imams) and the inner reality of true iman (faith). The Imam affirms that mere declaration of wilayah does not automatically confer upon a person the station of a Momin (true believer). However, he acknowledges that such people have been divinely ordained as a source of comfort and companionship for the genuine Momineen.

en.hubeali:
Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘
Not everyone who speaks as being with ourasws Wilayah is a Momin. But, it has been Made to be a comfort for the Momineen’.
en.sarwar: 7. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah from Ali ibn Ja’far who has said the following: “
Not everyone who speaks of our Walayah (Divine Authority) is a believer. They, however, are made to serve as boasting morals of the believing people.’”
